angle_title: Dil Kaybı: Hangi Atasözleri Ortadan Kayboluyor?

C1_adversarial_verification.objective: Each claim challenged with counter-evidence and alternative interpretations

findings.original_claim: Her iki haftada bir dil yok oluyor (One language every 2 weeks)

challenge.counterargument: The 'one language every 2 weeks' figure is widely cited but lacks robust empirical basis
challenge.evidence: ELCat (Endangered Languages Catalogue) estimates ~3.5 languages extinct per year (1 every 4 months), not every 2 weeks
challenge.alternative_metric: One language dies every 40 days (per LingoBright 2026 data) = ~9 languages/year
challenge.implication: The popular figure may be an overestimate or conflates 'language death' with 'serious endangerment'

findings.verdict: CLAIM AMENDED: Use 'one language every 40 days' or '~10 languages per year' rather than 'every 2 weeks'

challenge.consideration: Does UNESCO's 15-language count include regional minorities, immigrant communities, or only heritage languages?
challenge.finding: Yes - UNESCO list includes Zazaki, Laz, Pontus Greek, Armenian, Gagavuz, Assryian, and others reflecting Turkey's genuine linguistic diversity
challenge.alternative_perspective: Some sources cite higher numbers when including smaller immigrant/refugee communities
challenge.robustness: UNESCO figure is conservative but well-documented

findings.verdict: CONFIRMED: 15+ is accurate; may be conservative estimate

challenge.caveat: Projections are model-dependent and assume current conditions continue unchanged
challenge.counterargument: Language revitalization efforts (Wikitongues, UNESCO programs, community initiatives) could reduce extinction rates
challenge.alternative_scenario: If preservation efforts scale up, actual 2100 language loss could be 20-40% instead of 50-90%
challenge.uncertainty: Projection models do not account for future policy changes or technology-enabled language preservation

findings.verdict: PROJECTION CONFIRMED but assumes status quo; not deterministic

challenge.consideration: Some proverbs survive in literary form or through diaspora communities even after language death
challenge.counterexample: Latin proverbs survive in English, French, etc. despite Latin not being native language
challenge.nuance: Language death typically entails major loss of contextual/cultural proverb understanding even if verbal forms survive
challenge.verdict: Connection is robust but not absolute - some forms of transmission may persist

findings.verdict: CONFIRMED: Language death strongly correlates with proverb tradition loss, though some textual survival possible

findings.original_claim: Uyghur dili ve atasözleri tehlike altında (Uyghur language and proverbs under threat)

challenge.concern: Claims about Xinjiang policies are geopolitically sensitive and require careful sourcing
challenge.finding: Multiple independent sources (Diplomat, INALCO, Guardian, academic) confirm language displacement policies
challenge.counterargument: Chinese government maintains official support for minority languages, but practical education/media policies contradict this
challenge.classification: Well-documented but contested at policy level

findings.verdict: CONFIRMED: Uyghur under genuine threat from education/media policy shifts; proverb loss is real consequence

C2_historiography.objective: Examine different scholarly perspectives and traditions on language loss and proverb preservation

perspectives.name: Western Linguistic Endangerment Discourse
perspectives.characterization: Language death as crisis requiring intervention; endangerment metrics tied to speaker numbers and intergenerational transmission
assumptions: Death is inevitable without external intervention
limitations: May reflect Western values about language diversity
Doesn't account for multilingual communities' fluidity

perspectives.name: Indigenous Community Preservation Perspective
perspectives.characterization: Language vitality as embedded in cultural practice; revitalization through community action rather than external metrics
exemplars: Kazakh 'Words of the Ancestors' program (state+community partnership)
Kyrgyz oral tradition preservation through storytelling
assumptions: Communities know best how to preserve own languages
Cultural continuity matters more than speaker numbers
Language tied to land/heritage not abstract metrics

perspectives.name: Language Loss as Political Outcome
perspectives.characterization: Language death not 'natural' but policy-driven (Uyghur in China, Zazaki in Turkey, minority languages in Russia)
exemplars: Russian education policies post-Soviet (Tatar, minority Turkic languages)
assumptions: State language policy shapes speaker behavior
Language death often serves geopolitical goals
limitations: Can be politicized by different actors

perspectives.name: Turkic Oral Tradition Continuity
perspectives.characterization: Turkic proverbs (atasözleri) as sustained over centuries through nomadic/oral societies despite writing system changes
historical_arc: Pre-Islamic Turkic oral traditions (shamanism, ancestor wisdom)
Islamic period (proverbs adapted but core wisdom preserved)
exemplars: Kazakh 'Words of the Ancestors' project documents continuity
Kyrgyz Manas epic transmitted orally for centuries before written collection
Uyghur proverb collections (1800-proverb database) show textual archiving
assumptions: Turkic oral tradition is particularly resilient
Written documentation enables preservation of endangered forms
strengths: Explains why Turkic proverbs well-documented despite endangerment
Shows cultural pride in heritage (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan)
Demonstrates agency of communities in preservation
limitations: May overstate resilience - still losing speakers
Documentation not same as living tradition

C2_historiography.synthesis: No single narrative fully explains Turkic proverb endangerment. Political context (especially Uyghur case) drives urgency; Western endangerment discourse provides metrics; community initiatives provide agency; Turkic oral tradition history shows context for resilience.

C3_data_gaps.objective: Identify what we do NOT know and mark research frontiers

gaps.question: Which SPECIFIC Turkic proverbs have been lost due to language death? (vs. which still documented?)
gaps.current_state: We know language extinction happens and proverbs are endangered, but lack specific proverb inventories for pre-endangerment and current state
gaps.research_need: Comparative proverb corpora from Tuvan, Kazakh, Kyrgyz before/after language pressure
gaps.difficulty: HIGH - requires historical proverb collections vs. contemporary recordings

gaps.question: Are Uyghur proverbs still being transmitted orally to children despite Mandarin-dominant education?
gaps.current_state: We know 1800 Uyghur proverbs were collected (Abliz Emet 2013), but no recent data on intergenerational transmission rates
gaps.research_need: Ethnographic study of Uyghur youth language practices in Xinjiang 2020-2026
gaps.difficulty: EXTREMELY_HIGH - political sensitivity limits research access

gaps.question: Why is Kazakh proverb preservation apparently more successful than Kyrgyz or Uyghur?
gaps.current_state: Kazakh has 100-volume 'Words of the Ancestors' program; Kyrgyz has Manas epic protection; Uyghur has isolated collections. No comparative study of differential preservation success.
gaps.research_need: Institutional analysis of language policy differences; economic factors enabling documentation

gaps.question: What is the actual current rate of language extinction? (2 weeks vs. 40 days vs. 3 months?)
gaps.current_state: Conflicting data: ELCat (1 per 4 months), LingoBright (1 per 40 days), older claims (1 per 2 weeks). No consensus on measurement method.
gaps.research_need: Meta-analysis of extinction rate studies; standardized extinction definition across datasets

gaps.question: When a Turkic language nears extinction, what aspects of proverbs are MOST LOST - contextual meaning, poetic form, cultural referent, or all equally?
gaps.current_state: We know proverbs resist translation, but no systematic analysis of what fails first in endangered language contexts
gaps.research_need: Linguistic analysis of proverb degradation in late-speaker communities
gaps.difficulty: HIGH - requires access to endangered language communities

gaps.question: What is the actual impact of Wikitongues documentation on language preservation outcomes? (does documentation slow extinction?)
gaps.current_state: Wikitongues documented 776 languages but no outcome data on whether documented languages fare better in revitalization
gaps.research_need: Longitudinal study of language vitality trends for documented vs. undocumented languages

gaps.question: What Ottoman-era and medieval Turkish proverbs are now lost, and how do we know they existed?
gaps.current_state: We have Orkhon inscriptions, Ottoman defter records, and literary texts, but no inventory of 'missing' proverbs from earlier periods
gaps.research_need: Comparative analysis of proverb density in medieval texts vs. modern collections; etymological reconstruction

C5_source_quality_ranking.methodology: Ranked by authority, independence, methodological rigor, and recency

tier_1_authoritative.source: UNESCO Language Vitality and Endangerment Framework
tier_1_authoritative.uses: Defining language endangerment; metrics for vitality

tier_1_authoritative.independence: Non-profit linguistic reference (affiliated with SIL International)
tier_1_authoritative.uses: Speaker counts; endangerment metrics; comprehensive global baseline

tier_1_authoritative.rigor: Specialized extinction metrics; disputes popular claims
tier_1_authoritative.uses: Extinction rates; challenges to popular figures

tier_1_authoritative.rigor: Conservation biology methods applied to linguistics

tier_2_strong_secondary.independence: Community-led initiative with Library of Congress partnership
tier_2_strong_secondary.rigor: Grassroots documentation; not quantitatively rigorous but authentic
tier_2_strong_secondary.uses: Demonstration of active preservation; Turkic language documentation

tier_2_strong_secondary.independence: Mainstream media with science reporting credentials
tier_2_strong_secondary.uses: Reaching non-specialist audience; documentation scale numbers

tier_2_strong_secondary.independence: Kazakhstan-based cultural center (official but culturally grounded)
tier_2_strong_secondary.rigor: Institutional documentation; not peer-reviewed but authoritative on Kazakh culture
tier_2_strong_secondary.uses: Details on 'Words of Ancestors' program; Kazakh proverb preservation success

tier_3_useful_but_limited.caveat: Geopolitically charged; reflects critical perspective on Chinese policies

tier_3_useful_but_limited.rigor: Quality varies by author and journal publication
tier_3_useful_but_limited.uses: Specialized linguistic research on Turkic proverbs

tier_3_useful_but_limited.reliability: MEDIUM (useful for framing, not primary evidence)

tier_4_data_driven_but_commercial.uses: Extinction rate figure ('one language every 40 days')

most_reliable_for_claims: 2. ELCat via Rosetta Project (extinction rates, disputes popular figures)
sources_to_use_with_caution: Geopolitically sensitive sources about Uyghur (check multiple sources)
Blog articles (good for framing, not primary evidence)
summary_ranking.data_confidence_note: High confidence for 'language endangerment exists' and 'Turkic proverbs are documented'; medium confidence for exact extinction rates; medium-high confidence for political context of Uyghur/China policies.

key_amendments.from: One language dies every two weeks
key_amendments.to: One language dies every 40 days (~9-10 per year) or every 3-4 months depending on source

critical_data_gaps: Specific Turkic proverbs lost due to language death (vs. which remain documented)
Current Uyghur proverb intergenerational transmission rates in Xinjiang 2020-2026
Comparative analysis of why Kazakh preservation apparently more successful than Kyrgyz/Uyghur
Longitudinal impact of Wikitongues documentation on language revitalization outcomes
verification_summary.geopolitical_sensitivity: HIGH (Uyghur language politics, Turkish minority language policies, Xinjiang policies all touch sensitive issues)
